title: A lesson-only reply: a follow-up about how it went, tied to the lesson
origin: Issue #93 (spec example: discovery calls); Oct 30 live check on PR #90

answers.what: a small consulting side business for local gyms

history.text: Tonight, Riley: 7 pm at your desk, 15 minutes. Read the discovery-call article and write one opening question for a gym owner. Send a screenshot or a quick voice note when it's done.

plan.step: Write down 5 gyms near you you could talk to, at your desk
plan.destination: a first paying gym client by January

today_step.step: Read the discovery-call article and write one opening question for a gym owner, at your desk at 7 pm (15 min)

testerLines: [voice: Done. I learned discovery calls should start with their problem, not my pitch. I wrote my question: what's the hardest part of keeping members past month two?]
honestly it felt kind of awkward writing it, like I was guessing what they'd say
yeah I think talking to an actual owner would help
whatWentWrong: After a screenshot and a typed lesson, ZOH celebrated and went straight to tomorrow's step: it never learned how the step felt or what size suited them (Oct 30 live check).
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH counts the voice note and celebrates the lesson specifically. A lesson alone isn't how it went, so its question is about that, tied to what Riley said (did writing the question feel natural, or like pulling teeth?), never a list. It follows the awkwardness with at most one more specific question, then turns naturally to the next step: it acknowledges what Riley shared (it felt like guessing; a real owner would help) and proposes the next step day's step, fully defined (what, at the desk, 7 pm, 15 min), visibly using what Riley said (moving toward a real owner, or preparing for that), and asks if it works. One question per text. After "sounds good" it confirms in a line with no new question.
